a: Blockchain is a distributed ledger technology that records transactions across many computers so the record cannot be altered retroactively. Each block in the chain contains a set of transactions, a timestamp, and a cryptographic hash of the previous block, linking them together. This creates a chain of blocks that is transparent, decentralized, and tamper-resistant. Blockchain was first implemented in 2009 as the underlying technology for Bitcoin by the pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto. Beyond cryptocurrencies, blockchain has applications in supply chain tracking, digital identity, smart contracts (self-executing contracts on Ethereum), voting systems, and decentralized finance (DeFi). Key concepts include: consensus mechanisms (proof of work, proof of stake), mining (validating transactions), public vs private blockchains, and smart contracts.
